title: Thread a CancellationToken through the sync
summary: Add a CancellationToken after the fact, then settle how OperationCanceledException and a per warehouse timeout behave.

turns.user: the nightly sync worker never shuts down on deploy, we kill it every time. make it stop

assistant.body: SyncAllAsync never receives the stopping token, so every await inside it runs to the end no matter what the host does. Step 1: take a CancellationToken and pass it all the way down, from HttpClient to the store.

turns.user: it stops now. but every deploy floods the log with Error entries. a cancellation isn't a failure

assistant.body: Agreed, cooperative cancellation is the happy path. Let the exception keep propagating to the caller, and log it at Information instead. The when filter keeps the message honest by only claiming a host shutdown when the token we were handed is the one that fired. The loop body moves into SyncOneAsync unchanged.

turns.user: forgot to say, some warehouses hold 100k items and reading them in one go eats all the memory. page through them

assistant.body: Reading and storing stay separate: the read becomes an IAsyncEnumerable<StockItem>. An async iterator does not get the token on its own, so it takes one marked with EnumeratorCancellation and the caller feeds it through WithCancellation.

turns.user: also when one warehouse hangs the whole run is still going at breakfast. give up on a warehouse after 30 seconds and move on

assistant.body: Each warehouse gets its own source linked to the caller's token, with CancelAfter for the deadline. A warehouse that runs out of time is logged as a warning and the loop moves to the next one.

turns.user: doesn't that log timed out and carry on when the host shuts us down too? and 30 was too short, make it 90

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect on that catch. Without a filter it swallows the host shutdown as well. Adding when so it only catches while our own token is still unset leaves the shutdown to propagate. Both edits are one line each.
